build: PAL cassette in the KERNAL's own format, two files (AC, a BASIC boot; AZTEC, the game at $1000-$7FFE); the U.S. Gold release of Cosmi's tape as the Ultimate Tape Archive V4.0 has it (entry 733)

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's variables (levels, scores, counters, the tune's pointer) and the KERNAL's
runtime: the KERNAL's work area and vectors; the game writes only the interrupt vector at $0314
runtime: the screen and the sprite pointers; at the hand-over it still shows the boot program's title card, which the game clears
not the game's: BASIC's variables after the boot program and the power-on pattern of the RAM; nothing reads it
not the game's: the RAM under the KERNAL ROM, which the game never banks out; at $FD30 it holds a copy of the KERNAL's table of vectors, the same at the hand-over and in play

comments.text: Lives lost on the level being played, 0 to 5; also set to 4 for a preview, so its first loss ends it.
Player 1's level, as the digit character '1'-'7' ($31-$37), printed straight on the scorecard.
Player 2's level, as a digit character.
Player 1's phase, '1'-'4' as a digit character.
Player 2's phase, as a digit character.
The preview being played in the attract mode, 1-7; 0 in a real game.
The number of players, 1 or 2, from F1 or F3.
The player whose turn it is, '1' or '2' as a digit character.
The address a tune starts again from at its end mark, low byte then high ($30/$31).
Counts the interrupts down to the next step of the tune.
The offset of the next byte in the tune from $34/$35.
The tune being played, low byte then high ($34/$35).
The interrupts between two steps of the tune.
The progress stage within a level, 0 to 9: it moves the music on ($6530) and wins the level at its end.
The 16 settings of the current phase, $50-$5F, copied from $5C50-$5C8F as each level starts.
The phase's first colour (11, or 8 at night); the Piranha and the Bridge swap it with $5F as they start.
The phase's second colour (7, or 11 at night).
Player 1's score, eight BCD digits in four bytes, lowest first ($60-$63).
Player 2's score, $64-$67.
Achievements counted on this attempt, 10 points each when the attempt ends ($1456).

The boot program AC, ten lines of BASIC loaded from the tape and run by the KERNAL: it blacks the screen, prints Cosmi's title card with PRINT and TAB, loads the game file AZTEC to $1000 with LOAD"aztec",1,1, and, when the LOAD runs the program again from its first line, finds the game's first byte ($A2) at 4096 and starts it with SYS4096.

The game's first instruction (SYS 4096 from the BASIC boot), and where RUN/STOP comes back to (on the scorecard at $122B, and in the Vermin $66F8, the Stairs $6E09 and the Temple $76F3), as does the end of phase 4 ($1390, $13D2). Clears $D400-$D428 (the SID, and through its mirror at $D420 its first nine registers again) and loads $D400-$D418 from the 25 bytes at $41C0, points the interrupt vector $0314 at the music interrupt $1C00, sets the first tune ($5700, a step every 9 interrupts), blacks the screen and clears it through the KERNAL. Then the Cosmi logo: the spiral from $4000-$419F in light blue, in the multicolour characters at $3000; after a delay of 16x65536 loops, the sun stone from $4200-$43FF appears in orange a few characters at a time: 240 passes, each copying two characters at offsets picked at random by the CIA 1 timer A low byte, one from $4200 and one from $4300; then the whole of it. After two more delays the title, AZTEC from $4600 above it and CHALLENGE from $4700 below, in red. After a wait of 8x65536 increments it clears the screen, sets the main tune ($5F00, a step every 4 interrupts), turns all three voices on as triangle waves, sets the filter cutoff's high byte to $80 and the volume to 15, and goes to the menu at $1AF8.

Entered from the menu when F1 or F3 is pressed. Switches to the ROM character set, clears both scores ($60-$68), sets both players' level and phase digits ($03-$06) to '1' and makes player 1 current ($09), then falls into the scorecard.

The scorecard before every attempt, and where every level comes back to through $1300. Resets the stack, clears the lives lost ($02) and the preview number ($07), clears the screen, draws the labels ($1530), prints both players' level and phase digits and both 8-digit BCD scores, and the current player's level instructions ($1480). Then loops: flashes the current player's digit and UP at $0529 (1 UP or 2 UP) between two long delays ($12D5); any stick direction or fire on port 2 starts the level at $122E, and RUN/STOP restarts the game at $1000.

Fire was pressed on the scorecard. Turns off sprite expansion, priority, the ninth X bit and multicolour, clears the progress stage ($45) and the work bytes $10-$2F, copies the current player's phase table (16 bytes from $5C50, $5C60, $5C70 or $5C80 by the phase digit) to $50-$5F, and jumps to the current player's level by its digit: '1' $6000, '2' $6CF5, '3' $7600, '4' $6595, '5' $7200, '6' $7E98, anything else $7B00.
Four NOP bytes after the level dispatch; nothing jumps here.
A delay of 256x256 DEY loops, about a third of a second; used twice per pass of the scorecard loop, which is why fire must be held there.
32 NOP bytes; nothing runs them.

Every level ends here, won or lost, and so does each preview in the attract mode. Restores the ROM character set and the plain screen, turns off every sprite and the expansions, clears the collision latch, resets the tune to $5F00 every 4 interrupts with all three voices on as triangle waves. A preview ($07 set) goes on to the next one at $1B09. Otherwise: with five lives lost ($02 = 5) the player only gets 10 points for each achievement counted in $68 ($1456) and stays on the level; any fewer means the level was won, so the bonus for the lives lost ($1400) is added, the level digit steps on and after '7' wraps to '1' with the phase digit stepped on; past phase '4' the game restarts at $1000. With two players ($08 = 2) the turn passes to the other player first, whatever happened. Back to the scorecard at $1195.
40 zero bytes after level_over; nothing reads them.

Adds the win bonus to the score of the player X points at (0 player 1, 4 player 2), in decimal mode, by the lives lost in $02: 0 lost adds 10 hundreds (1000 points), 1 adds 800, 2 adds 600, 3 adds 400, 4 adds 200; then clears $02 and falls into $1456.
Adds 10 points to the score at $60,X once more than the count in $68 (so one extra 10 whenever it runs), in decimal mode, then clears $68 and $02. Entered on its own when the five lives are used up.
Four zero bytes after add_achievements; nothing reads them.
Copies the current player's level instructions, 160 bytes (four rows) from $1600 + 160 x (level-1), to the screen from $06A8 (row 17).
Six zero bytes after show_instructions; nothing reads them.
Draws the menu: "SELECT -" in light red at $047B, then "ONE PLAYER - PRESS KEY F1" in green and "TWO PLAYERS- PRESS KEY F3" in cyan below it, from the text at $5D40.
Four zero bytes after show_menu; nothing reads them.

Fills colour RAM with white, then writes the scorecard's labels from $5D7B-$5DBF: "PLAYER 1" and "PLAYER 2" in yellow and light blue, "LEVEL", "PHASE" and "SCORE" in two columns, alternating orange and cyan rows, and "PRESS FIRE BUTTON TO START" in light red on row 23.
78 zero bytes before the instruction text; nothing reads them.
The zero byte before the Gauntlet's text; $1494 reads from here plus X, with X from 160 down to 1, so this byte itself is never read.

The Gauntlet's instructions for the scorecard, four rows of 40 screen codes: THE GAUNTLET, then RUN TOWARD THE TEMPLE DODGING SPEARS THROWN FROM EITHER SIDE. PULL BACK ON THE STICK TO DUCK, PUSH FORWARD TO JUMP.
The last character of the Gauntlet's text, and the base $14A4 reads the Stairs' text from, plus 160 down to 1.
The Stairs' instructions, four rows: THE STAIRS, RUN UP THE STAIRS OF THE TEMPLE WHILE STONE BLOCKS ARE ROLLED DOWN AT YOU. PUSH LEFT & RIGHT ON THE STICK TO MOVE.
The last character of the Stairs' text, and the base $14B4 reads the Temple's text from.
The Temple's instructions: THE TEMPLE, ENTER THE TEMPLE THROUGH A SERIES OF ROOMS PROTECTED BY VARIOUS DEVICES. HOLD STICK LEFT TO STOP, RIGHT TO JUMP.
The last character of the Temple's text, and the base $14C4 reads the Vermin's text from.
The Vermin's instructions: THE VERMIN, PASS THRU THE DARK HEART OF THE TEMPLE AVOIDING THE FRIENDLY FAUNA OF MEXICO. PUSH UP FOR HIGH JUMPS, BACK FOR LOW.
The last character of the Vermin's text, and the base $14D4 reads Hopaztec's text from.
Hopaztec's instructions: HOPAZTEC, THE EXIT FROM THE TEMPLE IS COVERED WITH BOOBY-TRAPPED TILES. JUMP FORWARD, BACK OR SIDEWAYS TO FIND A SAFE PATH ACROSS.
The last character of Hopaztec's text, and the base $14E4 reads the Piranha's text from.
The Piranha's instructions: PIRANHA, SWIM THE LAKE IN ANY DIRECTION AND DIVE (FIRE BUTTON) FOR A SECOND TO AVOID THE MAN-EATING FISH. BUT KEEP GOING FORWARD.
The last character of the Piranha's text, and the base $14F0 reads the Bridge's text from.
The Bridge's instructions: THE BRIDGE, FREEDOM IS A HOP,SKIP & JUMP AWAY ACROSS A NARROW BRIDGE OVER A DEEP RAVINE. BACK IS A LOW JUMP,LEFT--MEDIUM,FORWARD-HIGH.
Sixteen zero bytes after text_bridge; nothing reads them.

Hopaztec's stand-in for the stick when nobody touches it: in a preview ($07 set) it takes a random direction from the low four bits of voice 3's oscillator and goes on to the hop at $7336, so the preview hops about by itself; in a real game it returns and the hopper waits.
Three zero bytes after hop_preview_stick; nothing reads them.

Hopaztec won: the hopper (shapes $B7/$B8) climbs diagonally up and to the right, a pixel each way 65 times with a delay, going behind the scenery for the last 49 steps (sprite priority $03 from the 17th step), into the doorway; then the level ends at $1300.
Three zero bytes after hop_exit; nothing reads them.

The Piranha, once per row of water drawn. While the swimmer (sprite 0) is between lines $34 and $DF it goes on to the bite check at $1EA0. Above or below that band the swimmer is passing off the edge of the lake and wraps round (sprite Y counts round 256); the first row of each passage ($2E clear) counts it, unless the stick is held down ($37 = 2): one more in $68, and every second one the progress stage $45 goes up with the music ($6530). Stage 9 wins the level ($1DD5).
Eleven zero bytes; nothing reads them.

The menu, and the attract mode between previews. Clears the preview number ($07), switches to the ROM character set, copies phase 1's table to $50-$5F, sets four lives lost ($02 = 4, so the preview ends at its first lost life) and draws the menu ($1500). Then waits about 65,536 passes for a key through the KERNAL's GETIN: F1 ($85) sets one player ($08 = 1), F3 ($86) two, and both start at $115B. With no key it plays the next preview: $07 counts 1 to 7 and jumps to that level's start (the Gauntlet, the Stairs, the Temple, the Vermin, Hopaztec, the Piranha, the Bridge); every level ends at $1300, which comes back to $1B09 while $07 is set; after the seventh the count starts again.
Five zero bytes after menu; nothing reads them.

The swimmer has been eaten (from $1F9D). All three voices to noise, then 64 times ($28 counts up from $C0): fills the 25 rows with random water characters from $4FF0 with the short delay ($7F61) after each, sets the three voices' pitch from voice 3's oscillator after each row, and jiggles the fish ($1FC6). Then falls into $1BD2.

A life lost on the Piranha, drowned or eaten. Restarts the tune ($1CA0) and counts the life ($02); the fifth ends the level at $1300. Otherwise takes every sprite off, waits and restarts the level at $7E9B, skipping the colour toggle.
Five zero bytes after piranha_lost; nothing reads them.

The game's interrupt, through $0314 from the KERNAL's timer interrupt, which it hands on to at $EA31 to keep the clock and the keyboard. Every $36 interrupts (the tempo, counted in $32) it plays one step of the tune at ($34),$33: six bytes, the frequency high and low byte of voice 1, voice 2 and voice 3, written straight into the SID. The voices' waveforms and envelopes are set elsewhere; the tune only moves the pitches. A byte $FF anywhere ends the tune and it starts again from the address in $30/$31 ($1C87). Writes $10 to $D01A each time.
The tune reached a byte $FF: starts it again from the address in $30/$31 (where $6530 may have put a new one), then hands on to the KERNAL's interrupt at $EA31.
Five zero bytes after music_loop; nothing reads them.
Puts the music back to its start for a new attempt: the tune at $5F00, a step every 4 interrupts, all three voices on as triangle waves, and the progress stage $45 cleared.

Swaps the Piranha's two colour bytes $5E/$5F, once as the level starts: in phases 1-3 ($5E = 11) the fish become brown (9) on a blue lake (6); in phase 4 ($5E = 8) the fish are dark grey (11) on black, the lake at night.

The Bridge's colour bytes, once as the level starts: in phases 1-3 ($5E = 11) the planks green (5), the picture's characters marked with bit 7 cyan (3) and the background white; in phase 4 the planks dark grey (11), those characters black and the background dark grey, at night.
Six zero bytes after bridge_colours; nothing reads them.

Moves the six fish (sprites 2-7) every $59 calls (the phase's fish delay, 5 in phase 1 down to 2): sprites 2, 3 and 4 swim right 2, 4 and 3 pixels a step ($1D64), sprites 5, 6 and 7 swim left 4, 2 and 3 pixels ($1D92), each with its bit masks for the ninth X bit in $28/$29. A fish that leaves the screen comes back on the other side at a random height from the CIA 1 timer.
Moves the fish in sprite 2+X/2 right Y+1 pixels; past X 352 (ninth bit set and X $60) it starts again at the left edge at a random height.
Moves the fish in sprite 5+X/2 left Y+1 pixels; past the left edge it starts again at X 352 at a random height.
Flips the ninth X bit of the sprite whose bit is in $28 (and its inverse in $29) in $D010.
Three zero bytes after flip_x9; nothing reads them.
The Piranha won: drops the return address and ends the level at $1300.
Three zero bytes after piranha_won; nothing reads them.
Stick centred: back to the surface at $7FB5.

The swimmer's stick, every second row: centred surfaces the swimmer ($7FB5); fire alone dives ($7F9D); up, down, left, right and the four diagonals move sprites 0 and 1 a pixel that way, left and right stopping at the screen's edges. Fire with a direction is none of these and does nothing. In a preview, $7FC4 enters at $1DE7 with a random direction.
Moves the swimmer (sprites 0 and 1) up a line. Also called for the diagonals up-left and up-right.
Moves the swimmer down a line. Also called for the diagonals down-left and down-right.
Moves the swimmer a pixel left, clearing both halves' ninth X bits when X wraps; refused at the left edge (X below 16 with the ninth bit clear).

Moves the swimmer a pixel right, setting both halves' ninth X bits when X wraps; refused at the right edge (X 320 and more). The rest of the routine is the stick's dispatch: 5 and 6 are left with up or down, 9 and 10 right with up or down.
Five zero bytes after swim_right; nothing reads them.

Fire is held: reads the sprite collision latch 129 times to empty it and returns, so nothing can bite a diving swimmer. This tests only the fire bit, so fire held with a direction, which does not dive and does not count toward drowning, protects the swimmer too.

The bite check: with fire held the swimmer is safe ($1E97). Otherwise, if the swimmer's upper half (sprite 0) touches a fish, every fish (sprites 1-7 in turn, though 1 is the swimmer's lower half) swims a pixel toward it, with a delay ($1F8E) after each, until all of them have reached the swimmer's position ($1F62); then $1F9D.
A delay of 6x6 counts between two fish moving in on the swimmer.
Every sprite becomes shape $BF in cyan, double size and single colour, a cloud where the swimmer was; then $1B80.
Two zero bytes after piranha_cloud; nothing reads them.
Every sixth call, moves each of the 16 sprite position registers $D000-$D00F one step up or down by a bit of the CIA 1 timer, so the cloud of fish shakes.
Three zero bytes after fish_jiggle; nothing reads them.

After a hop: unless the hopper is on the door's tile ($16 = 44), looks for the tile number in the list of trapped tiles at $5C28, the first $58 entries (the phase's count: 10, 16, 24 or 32). A match sets $15 = $AA, and the hopper is hit ($7502).
Two zero bytes after hop_trap; nothing reads them.

Sprite shapes $80-$8F, 64 bytes each, all multicolour: the runner seen from behind for the Gauntlet, each pose an upper and a lower half: running $80/$81 and $82/$83, jumping $84/$85, ducking $86/$87 and $88/$89; the spears $8A (flying right) and $8B (flying left), single colour, also Hopaztec's; falling $8C/$8D and lying $8E/$8F, which the Vermin and Hopaztec use too.

Shapes $90-$9F: the runner from the side for the Vermin, the Temple and the Bridge, running $90/$91, $92/$93, $94/$95, rising $96/$97, coming down $98/$99; the Vermin's creatures, a scorpion $9A, a spider $9B, a coiled snake $9C, a snake falling straight $9D and a long crawling creature $9E (a lizard or a crocodile, by its look); and $9F, one half of the runner lying down.

Shapes $A0-$AF: $A0, the other half of the runner lying down; the swimmer's two halves $A1/$A2 in the Piranha, its legs in the splashing water; the climber from behind for the Stairs, four poses $A3/$A4 to $A9/$AA; the rolling stone block in three turns $AB, $AC, $AD; and the flattened climber $AE/$AF.

Shapes $B0-$BF: $B0 the runner falling through the Bridge; $B1 a piranha; $B2 another fish, which no routine sets; $B3 a whole plank of the bridge and $B4 one with a hole; the hopper $B5/$B6 standing and $B7/$B8 jumping; $B9 a spear falling point down in the Temple; $BA a diagonal spear, which no routine sets; the swimmer's other stroke $BB/$BC; the Temple's spikes $BD and trapdoor $BE; and $BF, the cloud of blood where the swimmer was eaten.

Characters 0-127 of the set at $3000 (the menu's title and logo, the Temple, Hopaztec, the Piranha and the Bridge), multicolour: 0-143 draw Cosmi's spiral (the screen at $4000); the Bridge's gorge is drawn with characters 1-127 of the same, the spiral's swirls doing for rock.

Characters 128-255 of the set at $3000: 128-143 the end of the spiral; 144-215 the sun stone (the screen at $4200); 217-224 the Temple's pillars; 220-221 and 224-225 Hopaztec's walls and 233-236 its tiles' faces; 226-229 the ripples of the lake and the Bridge's foam; 230 the solid block the title's letters are built from; 42 is the floor of the Temple and Hopaztec.

Characters 0-127 of the set at $3800 (the Gauntlet, the Stairs and the Vermin), multicolour: most of 1-127 build the two rows of spear throwers in their five frames ($5000-$54AF); 103 is the Vermin's wall and 126 its ground; 121-123 the Gauntlet's sand, which the Stairs use for their steps with 127; 124-125 the temple ahead in the Gauntlet.
Characters 128-255 of the set at $3800: more of the spear throwers (129-247); 250-253 the doorway of the temple in the Gauntlet ($6331) and 252 also in the Stairs' steps; 254-255 the temple's top.
Cosmi's logo, the spiral, as 416 screen codes copied to $0528-$06C7 (from row 7, column 16): characters 0-143 of the set at $3000. $1000 copies 256 bytes from here and 160 from $4100.
The rest of the spiral, 160 bytes copied to $0628 by $106D; the 32 bytes after it ($41A0-$41BF) are $FF filler that nothing reads.

The 25 values $1000 writes to the SID's registers $D400-$D418 at start-up, seven for each voice (frequency low and high, pulse width low and high, control, attack/decay, sustain/release), then the filter and the volume: every voice at frequency 0 with attack 0, decay 8, sustain 8 and release 0; voices 1 and 2 sawtooth with the gate on ($21), voice 3 triangle ($11); pulse widths $8080, $F0F0 and $8080, which only a pulse wave would use; filter cutoff and resonance 0, volume 15.

The Piranha's sprite positions at the start, X then Y for sprites 0-7, which $7E9B copies to $D000-$D00F: the swimmer's halves at X 160, Y 171 and 192; the fish swimming right (sprites 2-4) at the left edge, Y 58, 122 and 186; the fish swimming left (sprites 5-7) at X 96, which the ninth X bits $E0 make 352, Y 90, 154 and 218.
The sun stone: 512 screen codes (characters 144-215 of the set at $3000, and spaces) copied to $0528-$0727, from row 7 column 16, by the logo at $1000 and on the back wall of the Temple ($7808).
The second half of the sun stone, copied to $0628: a character at a time at random by $10AA, then whole by $10CB in the logo, and by $7816 for the Temple.
The Temple's left pillar: 22 rows of three screen codes, which $7600 draws down columns 0-2 from the top.
The Temple's right pillar: 22 rows of three, drawn down columns 37-39.

The colours a Temple room flashes when the runner leaves it, four at a time into the border and the three background colours $D020-$D023: eight sets of four, one set a room, round again after the eighth.

320 bytes nothing reads: zeros, then a run of screen codes $9F, $C2 and spaces in blocks of five ($44FE-$4579), then 52 bytes ($457A-$45AD) of values such as $20, $48, $70, $98, $C0, $E8 and $3A, $62, $8A, $B2, $DA, spaced $28 apart like positions in pixels, then $FF filler and zeros. No instruction or pointer reaches them; what they were for is not known.
The title's AZTEC: 200 screen codes (five rows of 40) of the solid character 230 and spaces, drawn in red at the top ($0428) by $10F0 after the logo.
The title's CHALLENGE: 200 screen codes drawn in red at $06F8, below the sun stone. The 56 bytes after each of the two (spaces) are not read.

The Stairs' steps, three rows of 40 screen codes (sand characters 121-123, 127 and 252), repeated down the screen by $6E90, $6F10 and $6F80; after it 48 spaces, $FF filler and zeros that nothing reads.

The fourth stage's tune ($6530 points the loop at it): steps of six bytes, the high and low frequency bytes of voices 1, 2 and 3, 127 whole steps and four bytes of another before the $FF at $4BFE; a step every 10 interrupts.

The Bridge's gorge, 1000 screen codes for the whole screen: the low seven bits are the character (from the set at $3000), and bit 7 says which colour $7B57 gives it: set, the phase's colour $5F; clear, brown.
The second 256 bytes of the Bridge's picture, for screen page $0500.
The third 256 bytes of the Bridge's picture, for screen page $0600.
The last 232 bytes of the Bridge's picture, for $0700-$07E7, and eight zeros after it.
The eight characters the lake and the eaten swimmer's whirl are drawn with, picked at random by the CIA 1 timer's low three bits: 226, 229, 227, 228, 229, 226, 227, 228; then eight zeros.
The Gauntlet's two rows of spear throwers, frame 1 of 5: 240 screen codes for rows 14-19 ($0630) in the set at $3800.
The throwers, frame 2 of 5, drawn after the first by $60FA.
The throwers, frame 3 of 5.
The throwers, frame 4 of 5.
The throwers, frame 5 of 5, the last before the loop draws frame 1 again; after it, 64 sand characters ($54B0-$54EF) and zeros that nothing reads.

The temple ahead in the Gauntlet, the even stages: rows of 40 screen codes, characters 124-125 for its sides, 254-255 for the middle of the top, of which $62E0 copies as many bytes as $44 says, a whole row more each odd stage, as the temple grows.
The temple's odd stages, read by $62E0 like $5500; the eight bytes of 42 at $56F8 are not read.

The title tune, and the third stage's: 41 whole steps of six bytes (voices 1-3, high byte first) and four bytes of another before the $FF at $57FA; a step every 9 interrupts at the title, every 8 as the third stage.
Hopaztec's room, 1000 screen codes for the whole screen in the set at $3000: the walls, the floor of tiles and the doorway at the top right.
The second 256 bytes of Hopaztec's room, for $0500.
The third 256 bytes of Hopaztec's room, for $0600.
The last 232 bytes of Hopaztec's room, for $0700-$07E7.
The six X positions of the hopper on the back row (Y $46) where a forward hop is refused: $82, $AA, $D2, $FA, $22, $4A; then two zeros.
The eight X positions on the front row (Y $C6) where a back hop is refused.
The nine rows of tiles, the hopper's Y from $46 to $C6 in steps of 16, which the side checks pair with $5C08 and $5C18.

For each of the nine rows in $5BF8, the X of the leftmost tile, where a hop to the left is refused: $82 on the back row, 16 pixels further left each row nearer the front, and $2A, the start, on the front row.
For each of the nine rows, the low byte of the X of the rightmost tile, where a hop to the right is refused; the check compares only this byte with the hopper's X.

The trapped tiles of this attempt: up to 32 tile numbers, written by $74C2 at the start of Hopaztec and read by $1FE8 after every hop. The bytes in the file are whatever the list held when the program was saved; the game writes its own before reading.

The 16 settings of phase 1, copied to $50-$5F as a level starts: $50 the Gauntlet's wait between spears, $51 its spear step delay, $52 its spear speed; $53-$55 the Stairs' three block speeds; $56 the Temple's rooms per stage; $57 the Vermin's spawn delay; $58 the number of trapped tiles; $59 the fish delay; $5A the Bridge's loop delay; $5B-$5D its low, middle and high jumps; $5E and $5F two colours (day: 11 and 7).

Phase 2's settings: the Gauntlet 2, 9, 5 (where phase 1 has 5, 5, 2); blocks 10, 12, 14; 2 rooms a stage; creatures every 80; 16 trapped tiles; fish every 4; the Bridge's delay 8 and jumps 17, 30, 42; colours 11 and 7.
Phase 3's settings: the Gauntlet 1, 4, 2; blocks 12, 14, 16; 4 rooms a stage; creatures every 48; 24 trapped tiles; fish every 3; the Bridge's delay 7, jumps 16, 29, 41; colours 11 and 7.

Phase 4's settings, at night: the Gauntlet 1, 4, 2 as phase 3; blocks 14, 16, 18; 6 rooms a stage; creatures every 16; 32 trapped tiles; fish every 2; the Bridge's delay 6, jumps 15, 28, 40; and the colours 8 and 11 (orange and dark grey) where the day has 11 and 7 (dark grey and yellow).

176 bytes nothing reads, between the phase settings and the menu's words: $FF filler and zeros, then at $5D00 forty screen codes, 42, 234, 236, 236 and 235 eight times over, the pattern of a row of Hopaztec's tiles (a gap, then a tile's face), which no routine draws; then $FF filler.

The menu's and the scorecard's words, in screen codes: SELECT - ($5D40), ONE PLAYER - PRESS KEY F1 ($5D48), TWO PLAYERS- PRESS KEY F3 ($5D61), LEVEL ($5D7B), PHASE ($5D80), SCORE ($5D85), PRESS FIRE BUTTON TO START ($5D8A), PLAYER 1 ($5DA4) and PLAYER 2 ($5DAC).
ONE PLAYER - PRESS KEY F1, 25 screen codes, drawn in green by $1500.
TWO PLAYERS- PRESS KEY F3, 25 screen codes, drawn in cyan by $1500; the space after it is not read.
LEVEL, five screen codes, written twice on the scorecard by $1530.
PHASE, five screen codes, written twice by $1530.
SCORE, five screen codes, written twice by $1530.
PRESS FIRE BUTTON TO START, 26 screen codes, on row 23 of the scorecard.
PLAYER 1, eight screen codes, in yellow at the left of the scorecard.
PLAYER 2, eight screen codes, in light blue at the right; the $FF bytes after it are not read.

The tune of the menu and of every level's start: seven steps of six bytes and five of another, then $FF at $5F2F, a step every 4 interrupts: pitches $0100, $0200 and $0390 on the three voices (a few hertz, a low pulse) between steps of silence, round and round.
The melody that follows the pulse, from the second stage ($6530 starts the loop here): 31 whole steps of six bytes (voices 1-3, high byte first) and five bytes of another before the $FF at $5FEF.
Sixteen zero bytes after tune_a2; nothing reads them.

Level 1, the Gauntlet, and where it restarts after a lost life. Clears the screen to character 0 in the phase's colour ($5E) on the phase's background ($5F: yellow sand in phases 1-3, dark grey at night in phase 4), puts the runner (sprites 0 and 1, the upper and lower half, shapes $80/$81) at the bottom centre, multicoloured, sets the throwers' spears (sprites 2 and 3, shapes $8A/$8B, black, behind the scenery, double width, both with the ninth X bit), restarts the tune ($1CA0), draws the first stage of the temple ($62E0), and switches to the multicolour characters at $3800. Then the main loop: draws the five frames of the two rows of spear throwers from $5000, $50F0, $51E0, $52D0 and $53C0 (240 bytes each) over rows 14-19 one after another, with a ground scroll ($616B) after each of the first four, then serves the spears ($634E) and the music ($6530). A stick held in any direction (or fire) for 8 passes of this loop running makes the runner fall ($6470): the manual's "staying in either mode for too long".
One zero byte between two routines; nothing reads it.

One step of the Gauntlet between two thrower frames: waits 44x44 counts, serving the spears ($634E) on each of the 44; scrolls the sand of rows 20-24 down a row and fills row 20 with sand characters $79, $7A or $7B picked by the CIA 1 timer; then copies a trapezoid of rows 15-23 down a row, each row up a character narrower on each side, so the ground comes toward the player in perspective. Every 88 steps ($46) the temple grows a stage ($62E0); the call after stage 8 wins the level. Then the runner: up (forward on the stick) starts a jump ($47 = 1, shapes $84/$85), down starts a duck ($48 = 1); a jump rises 9 lines a step to line $A8 and falls back to $C8 ($6250); a duck holds the crouching shapes $86/$87 and $88/$89 in turn for 4 steps ($6290); otherwise the running shapes $80/$81 and $82/$83 alternate ($62C0).
Three zero bytes after gauntlet_frame; nothing reads them.

One step of the runner's jump: rising ($47 = 1) moves sprites 0 and 1 up 9 lines until line $A8, then sets $47 = 2 and the standing shapes; falling moves them down 9 lines until line $C8, then clears $47.
Two zero bytes after gauntlet_jump; nothing reads them.
One step of the duck: swaps the runner between the two crouching shape pairs $86/$87 and $88/$89; after 4 steps ($49) clears the duck flag $48.
Five zero bytes after gauntlet_duck; nothing reads them.
One step of the run: swaps the runner between the shape pairs $80/$81 and $82/$83.
Three zero bytes after gauntlet_run; nothing reads them.

Draws the next stage of the temple ahead, by the progress stage $45: an even stage copies a row from $5500, an odd one from $5600, $44 characters long in the phase's colour, at the screen address in $40/$41; after stages 1, 3 and 5 the next copy is 40 characters longer and starts a row higher. Stage 7 instead puts the temple's doorway, characters $FA-$FD, at $061A, and $45 is then 8. Called once more at stage 8, it ends the level as won: drops two return addresses and jumps to $1300.

Serves the spears, called many times a step. With no spear in flight ($20 = 0) it counts down a two-byte wait ($15/$16) from the phase's $50; when it runs out it throws one, from the left ($20 = 1, sprite 2) or the right ($20 = 2, sprite 3) by the CIA 1 timer's low bit, at head height (line $CE) or at the feet (line $E0) by a bit of voice 3's oscillator, and starts the whoosh on voice 1 (noise, pitch $F0). In flight, every $51 calls it moves the spear ($63D0) and then reads the sprite collision latch: a value from 5 to 11 means the runner's sprites touched a spear, and the runner falls ($6470).
Four NOP bytes after gauntlet_spears; nothing runs them.

Moves the spear in flight $52+1 pixels across the screen (sprite 2 to the right, sprite 3 to the left, carrying the ninth X bit through $6430/$6450), lowering the whoosh's pitch a step each time. When it reaches the other side it ends the throw: clears $20, silences voice 1's pitch, sets it back to a sawtooth, and counts a dodged spear in $68 (10 points at the end).
Seven zero bytes after spear_move; nothing reads them.
Sprite 2's X position wrapped past 255: flips its ninth X bit in $D010 and steps it once more.
Two NOP bytes after spear2_carry; nothing runs them.
Sprite 3's X position wrapped past 0: flips its ninth X bit in $D010 and steps it once more.
A NOP and a zero byte; nothing runs them.

The runner is down, hit by a spear or held too long. Sets voice 1 to noise at a low pitch, shows the falling shapes $8C/$8D and slides the runner and the spear 32 pixels away from the side the spear came from, 16 lines down, then the lying shapes $8E/$8F; waits, silences voice 1, takes the spears off and clears the jump and duck flags. Counts a life lost ($02): the fifth ends the level at $1300, otherwise the tune restarts and the level starts again at $6000.
Two zero bytes after gauntlet_fall; nothing reads them.
A delay of 40x40 counts, one step of the runner's fall.
One zero byte after delay_fall; nothing reads it.

Changes the music as the player gets on, by the progress stage $45, called each time a level moves it on. Stage 1 turns all three voices to sawtooth; stage 2 starts the loop of the tune from $5F30 and voice 2 on a sawtooth; stage 3 from $5700, a step every 8 interrupts, voice 3 on a triangle; stage 4 from $4900 (the start's low byte left at $00), every 10 interrupts, voice 3 off; stage 5 voice 3 on a triangle again; stage 6 voice 3 on a sawtooth. Stages 0, 7, 8 and 9 change nothing. A new start takes effect when the tune playing reaches its end mark ($1C87).
Ten zero bytes; nothing reads them.

Level 4, the Vermin, and where it restarts after a lost life. Clears the screen, fills the top of the screen with character $67 in cyan ($6CD0), puts the runner (sprites 0 and 1, shapes $90/$91, multicoloured) at the left, clears the progress stage, switches to the multicolour characters at $3800, and fills rows 15-24 with character $7E in light red. Then scrolls the ground to the left: it lowers the fine X scroll a pixel at a time, with a delay and a step of the creatures and the runner ($66AA) at each; at 0 it moves rows 15-23 left a character, puts $7E in the last column, sets the scroll back to 7, reads RUN/STOP (back to $1000) and counts the progress ($6AF1).
Two NOP bytes after vermin; nothing runs them.

Every third call: moves the creatures ($6700), the runner's jump ($6B10) and checks the bite ($6BE0). A bite that has lasted 8 steps ($16 set) kills the runner ($6C40). On the ground ($17 = 0), every third such step the runner's legs move: shapes $90/$91, $92/$93, $94/$95 in turn.
Two NOP bytes after vermin_step; nothing runs them.
After each character of scroll: updates the clock and reads the STOP key through the KERNAL; RUN/STOP restarts the game at $1000, otherwise on to the progress count at $6AF1.
Two zero bytes after vermin_stop; nothing reads them.

Every $57 calls (the phase's spawn delay: 128, 80, 48, 16) it brings on creatures: for each bit of the CIA 1 timer's low byte from 0 to 5 that is set, the creature of that bit is placed ($67A0-$683A) unless it is already out (its bit in $2A). For bit 4 the check ORs #$00 into $2A where the others OR in their own bit ($6772), so creature E is never marked as out: it is placed again each time and never moves. Then every creature that is out takes a step ($68F0).
Fourteen NOP bytes; nothing runs them.

Places creature A: sprite 2, shape $9A, orange, on the ground at line $B6, at X 256 plus a random byte (256-511): about a third of the time already on the right edge of the screen (up to 343), otherwise past it.
Places creature B: sprite 3, shape $9B, white, at line $B3, at X 256 plus a random byte (256-511): about a third of the time already on the right edge of the screen, otherwise past it.
Places creature C: sprite 4, shape $9B, yellow, at the top of the screen (line $10) at a random X on the left 256 pixels.
Two NOP bytes after creature_c; nothing runs them.
Places creature D: sprite 5, shape $9D, light red, double height, at the top (line $10) at a random X.

Places creature E: sprite 6, shape $9C, green, at line $AD, at X 256 plus a random byte. The check that calls it ($6772) ORs #$00 into $2A instead of creature E's bit, so its mover $6A80 never runs and its sprite is never switched on: creature E never appears.
Places creature F: sprite 7, shape $9E, medium grey, double width, at line $AA, at X 256 plus a random byte: sometimes already on the right edge of the screen, otherwise past it.

A second copy of the creature checks in $670B-$678F, without the spawn delay before them and ending in a jump to $68F0; nothing jumps or calls here, so it never runs. Its check for creature E has the same ORA #$00 ($68C7).
Nine NOP bytes after vermin_spawn_old; nothing reads them.
Moves each creature that is out, by its bit in $2A: A $6930, B $6965, C $69E0, D $6A30, E $6A80, F $6AC0.
Nine NOP bytes; nothing runs them.
Creature A crawls left 3 pixels; off the left edge, it is taken off (sprite 2 off, its bit in $2A cleared).
Four NOP bytes after move_a; nothing runs them.
Creature B moves left 3 pixels a step while it hops: up to line $90, then down to line $B0, and again ($2B says which way). Off the left edge it is taken off.
Sixteen NOP bytes after move_b; nothing runs them.
Creature C drops from the top diagonally, a line down and a pixel left four times a step, to the ground at line $B0, then runs left 3 pixels a step and is taken off at the left edge.
Sixteen NOP bytes after move_c; nothing runs them.
Creature D drops straight down 5 lines a step to the ground at line $B0, where it turns into shape $9C at normal height; then crawls left 3 pixels a step and is taken off at the left edge.
Three NOP bytes after move_d; nothing runs them.
Would move creature E left 3 pixels a step and take it off at the left edge. Nothing ever sets its bit in $2A ($681A), so it never runs.
Two zero bytes and thirteen NOPs; nothing runs them.
Creature F crawls left 3 pixels a step; off the left edge, it is taken off.
Counts the characters scrolled ($69); every 112 the progress stage $45 goes up and the music changes ($6530). At stage 9 the level is won ($6C23); otherwise back to the scroll at $662C.

The runner's jump. On the ground ($17 = 0), up on the stick starts a high jump ($17 = 2) and down a low one ($17 = 1). A low jump rises 4 lines a step to line $90, then ($17 = 3) falls 4 lines a step; a high jump rises 5 lines a step to line $70, then ($17 = 4) falls 6; both land at line $B0, back on the running shapes $90/$91. The jumping shapes are $96/$97, the falling ones $98/$99.
Five zero bytes after vermin_jump; nothing reads them.

Reads the sprite collision latch: while the runner's lower half (sprite 1) touches another sprite, counts the steps in $15 and an achievement in $68 each time; at 8 steps in a row it sets $16, the runner is bitten. A step without a touch clears $15. The manual's "do not touch any creature for more than a second".
Eight NOP bytes; nothing runs them.

After the bitten runner has fallen: waits, takes every creature off and counts a life lost ($02). Not the fifth: the tune restarts and the level starts again at $6595. The fifth, or the level won (entered at $6C23): drops a return address, divides the achievements counted in $68 by four, and ends the level at $1300.
Eight zero bytes after vermin_lost; nothing reads them.

The runner is bitten: falling shapes $8C/$8D sink to line $B8 while creatures C and D, if out, sink with it; then the lying shapes $A0/$9F; the two creatures go on sinking to line $B0; a delay, then $6C00.
Nine zero bytes after vermin_bitten; nothing reads them.
Fills the first 768 characters of the screen (rows 0-18 and the first eight of row 19, up to $06FF) with character $67 and their colour with cyan; the Vermin then covers rows 15 on with the ground.
Nine zero bytes after fill_wall; nothing reads them.

Level 2, the Stairs, and where it restarts after a lost life. Clears the collision latch and the screen, colours the screen white ($6E70) and draws the steps from $4800 ($6E9F). The climber is sprites 4 and 5 (shapes $A3/$A4, white, multicoloured, the two halves one above the other at X 144); the three stone blocks are sprites 0, 1 and 2 (shapes $AB-$AD, double size; 1 and 2 set to white, 0 keeps its colour) starting at the top at X 48, 96 and 160. Medium grey background, the multicolour characters at $3800, colour RAM light grey. Clearing the fine scroll also clears bit 3 of $D011: 24 rows are shown. Then the climb: the fine vertical scroll goes 0 to 7, a line at a time, with a delay and a move of the blocks ($7000) at each; at 7 the climber's legs move ($6E10) and the steps are drawn again one row lower in turn from three starting rows ($6E90, $6F10, $6F80), so they slide down the screen as the climber goes up; then the clock and the STOP key (RUN/STOP restarts at $1000).
Four NOP bytes after stairs; nothing runs them.

The climber's step: while $11 is clear both halves' shapes go up by 2 a call, $A3/$A4 to $A5/$A6, $A7/$A8 and $A9/$AA, then $11 is set and they come back down by 2 to $A3/$A4: four poses, forward and back.
Three zero bytes after stairs_legs; nothing reads them.

Counts the climb: $69 to 128, then the stage $6A and the music stage $45 go up together ($6530); eight of them win the level ($1300, dropping a return address). Every sixteenth count adds an achievement in $68. Then the stick at $70E0.
Four zero bytes after stairs_progress; nothing reads them.
Fills colour RAM ($D800-$DBE7) with white. Used by the Stairs and the Piranha.
Seven zero bytes after colour_white; nothing reads them.

Waits for raster line $F5, puts the fine vertical scroll back to 0, then draws the steps: the 120 bytes at $4800 (three rows) eight times from the top of the screen and its first row again on row 24. Entered at $6E9F (without the wait) to draw the first picture.
$6E90 without the wait for the raster line: draws the steps from the top row, as the Stairs start.
Thirteen bytes, a NOP and zeros; nothing runs them.
Waits for raster line $F5, puts the fine vertical scroll back to 0, and draws the three rows from $4800 eight times starting a row lower, at row 1.
Eight zero bytes after stairs_rows_b; nothing reads them.

Waits for raster line $F5, puts the fine vertical scroll back to 0, and draws the steps starting at row 2, with the last two rows from $4800 filling rows 23 and 24 and its first row on row 0, so the three pictures follow one another a row apart.
Four NOPs and nine zero bytes; nothing runs them.

Every third call moves the three blocks down: block 0 by $53+1 lines, block 1 by $54+1, block 2 by $55+1 (the phase's speeds: 7, 9 and 11 lines a step in phase 1, up to 15, 17 and 19 in phase 4), each turning through shapes $AB, $AC, $AD as it rolls. A block at or past line $F0 comes back in at the top: block 0 at the climber's X, aimed at the player; block 1 at a random X from the CIA 1 timer and block 2 from the CIA 2 timer, each given the ninth X bit at random when its X is below $50. Then $6E45.
Twelve zero bytes; nothing reads them.

Reads the collision latch: if the climber's upper half (sprite 4) touched a block, the climber is flattened (shapes $AE/$AF) and every block rolls on down off the bottom of the screen, 9 lines a step with a delay; a long wait, then a life lost ($02). The fifth halves the achievements in $68 and ends the level at $1300; otherwise the stage counters and the ninth X bits are cleared, the tune restarts and the level starts again at $6CF5. With no hit, the stick at $71A0.
Six zero bytes after stairs_hit; nothing reads them.

Moves the climber (sprites 4 and 5) 4 pixels a step: left for any input below 7, which is left and its diagonals but also up and down alone (stopping at X $34), and right for any input of 7 or more, which is right, its diagonals and anything with fire (stopping at X $12A).
Four zero bytes after stairs_stick; nothing reads them.

Level 5, Hopaztec (the Tiles). Black border, the multicolour characters at $3000, green and light green as the shared colours. Draws the room from the 1000 bytes at $5800-$5BE7: characters $E9-$EC (the tiles' faces) in yellow, everything else multicoloured with black. Colours the doorway's eight cells by the phase ($7724: cyan, or black at night). Puts the hopper at the start ($73F0), picks the trapped tiles ($74C2), then the loop: reads the stick and hops ($732A); a hop onto a trapped tile ($15 = $AA) brings a spear ($7502), counts a life lost and puts the hopper back at the start; the fifth ends the level at $1300. Reaching tile 44, the doorway, wins ($1A80).
The RTS that $732A's last test branches to when the stick holds a value with no hop.

Reads the stick: centred, $1A70 (waits, or a random hop in a preview). Up hops forward (tile +1, an achievement in $68) at $7430; down hops back (tile -1, and one achievement taken off) at $7450; left hops to the left (tile -9) at $7470; right to the right (tile +9) at $7493. Diagonals and fire do nothing.
The forward hop: 16 steps of a pixel right and a pixel up for both halves, with a delay ($73BE) after each, then $73A3.
The back hop: 16 steps of a pixel left and a pixel down, then $73A3.
The hop to the left: 40 steps of a pixel left, then $73A3.
The hop to the right: 40 steps of a pixel right, then $73A3.
Lands: the standing shapes $B5/$B6, waits for the stick to be let go, a short delay, then checks the tile ($1FE8).
A delay of 32x32 counts, then keeps the hopper's ninth X bit right: when the X of sprite 0 has just wrapped to 0, sets bits 0-1 of $D010 if they were clear and clears them if they were set.
Six zero bytes after hop_delay; nothing reads them.
Puts the hopper at the starting tile: shapes $B5/$B6 in white, multicoloured with brown and yellow, at X $2A, Y $C6 and $DB, both sprites on and the ninth X bits clear; the tile number $16 = 9.
Two zero bytes after hop_start; nothing reads them.
A forward hop from the back row (Y $46) is refused when X is one of the six in $5BE8, the room's edge there; otherwise the jumping shapes ($74B6), the tile +1 and the hop ($7356).
A back hop from the front row (Y $C6) is refused when X is one of the eight in $5BF0; otherwise the jumping shapes, the tile -1 and the hop ($736D).
A hop to the left is refused when the hopper's Y and X are one of the nine pairs in $5BF8 and $5C08, the left edge of the floor; otherwise the jumping shapes, the tile -9 and the hop ($7384).
A hop to the right is refused when Y and X are one of the nine pairs in $5BF8 and $5C18, the right edge; otherwise the jumping shapes, the tile +9 and the hop ($7395).
Sets the hopper's jumping shapes $B7/$B8.
One NOP byte after hop_shapes; nothing runs it.

Picks the trapped tiles for this attempt: writes $80 to voice 3's control (noise, gate off) and to its frequency's low byte (the high byte stays as the tune left it), and reads its oscillator, keeping values below $3C or from $3F to $42 (it refuses $3C-$3E and anything from $43; a test against 44 in the same chain can never match there), with a delay ($74EC) between picks, until $58 tile numbers are in $5C28 (10, 16, 24 or 32 by the phase). Then voice 3 back to a triangle. Numbers may repeat, and tile 44 (the doorway) may be picked, which $1FE8 never tests. These are the only bytes of the program the game writes.
A delay of 128x128 counts between two picks of a trapped tile, so the noise has moved on.
One zero byte after delay_pick; nothing reads it.

The hopper is on a trapped tile: a spear (sprite 2, shape $8A, black) flies in from the left edge at the hopper's height with a falling whoosh on voice 1 (noise), until it reaches the hopper; the hopper's falling shapes $8C/$8D; a second spear (shape $8B) from X 352 flies back from the right; then the shapes $88/$89, a low rumble, voice 1 back to a triangle, and the lying shapes $8E/$8F, with a last delay.
Two NOP bytes after hop_speared; nothing runs them.
A delay of 16x16 counts, one step of the spears.

The Temple: the runner went out of the right of a room. An achievement in $68; $69 counts the rooms, and every $56 (the phase's: 1, 2, 4 or 6) the stage $45 and the music go up ($6530); stage 9 wins ($1300, dropping a return address). Otherwise the next room ($7835).
One NOP byte after temple_room_done; nothing runs it.

Level 3, the Temple, and where it restarts after a lost life. Dark grey border on black; the first room's trap is the spears ($1A = 1); the runner (sprites 0 and 1, shapes $90/$91, yellow and white, multicoloured) at the left on the floor, $17 = 8 (standing); the sun stone from $4200 on the back wall ($7808); colour RAM light grey for the first 840 characters; the multicolour characters at $3000; the floor (character $2A, light green) on rows 21-24 ($0748-$07E7); the two pillars from $4400 and $4450, three characters wide, down the left and right edges. Then the loop: the runner ($7700), the trap ($785B), a delay, the STOP key (RUN/STOP restarts at $1000), and the bite of the trap ($79F0).
Seven NOP bytes; nothing runs them.

The runner: in a jump ($17 1 or 2) goes on with it ($77B0). Otherwise the stick: right (and anything of 8 or more: its diagonals, fire) starts a jump ($17 = 1); any other input stops the runner, which is the manual's "left to stop"; centred, it runs ($7732).
Four bytes after the JMP of the jump that no path reaches: CMP #$04 and BNE, the start of a test for the stick held left that the routine no longer has.
The RTS that stops the runner for any input below 8.
Colours the doorway's top left cell ($D84D) cyan, or black when A is 11 (the night of phase 4); returns with the colour in A, which $7200 then puts in the doorway's other cells.

Every fourth call the runner's legs move (shapes $90/$91, $92/$93, $94/$95 in turn); every call it runs 3 pixels right, carrying the ninth X bit. Off the right side (X 336 and more) the room is done: the border and the three background colours flash from the table at $44A0, four entries a room, and on to $75DB.
The RTS for the runner still inside the room.

The jump, for $17 = 1 rising 4 lines a step (shapes $96/$97) to line $A8, then $17 = 2 falling 4 lines a step (shapes $98/$99) to the floor at line $D5, back to standing ($17 = 8, shapes $90/$91); both go on moving right ($7758).
Four NOP bytes after temple_jump; nothing runs them.

Clears the screen through the KERNAL and copies the sun stone ($4200-$43FF) to $0528-$0727 (row 7, column 16, to row 20, column 7; the stone itself fills rows 7-17) in orange, then clears the ninth X bits, the room count $69 and the stage $45.
Four NOP bytes after temple_wall; nothing runs them.
The next room: picks the trap $1A at random from the CIA 1 timer, one of 1, 3, 5 or 7 (the low bit must be set); only the runner's sprites on, unexpanded, back at X 16 on the left.

Runs the room's trap by its state $1A. 1: six spears (sprites 2-7, shape $B9, white) and 5: six stones (shape $AB, yellow) are lined up at the top ($7870), state 2 or 6. 2 and 6: they fall one at a time, 9 lines a step, each from a random X, and when the sixth is down the state goes back to 1 or 5, so they keep falling. 3: three spikes (shape $BD) under the floor at X 80, 160 and 255, state 4: they rise one after another, 3, 4 and 4 lines a step, until each is above line $D5. 7: three trapdoors (shape $BE, black, double height) in the floor at X 96, 192 and 288, state 8: the first opens (comes on) 16 calls after they are set, the next two 32 calls apart.

Lines up the six falling things at the top left (all their positions 0), with $1B the one to drop first and $1C its bit for the ninth X; the state goes on to 2 or 6 and every sprite comes on. Its $7887-$7889 are $1A $04 $D0, two NOPs of the processor's undocumented set (one of a byte, one of two) after reading the CIA 1 timer, which leave nothing changed; what they replaced is not known.

Drops the faller in $1B 9 lines a step; when it passes line $EA its shape moves on one, and the next faller gets a random X (from the CIA 1 timer, with the ninth bit when below $40). After the sixth, the state goes back one, to 1 or 5, to start again.
Three NOP bytes after temple_fall; nothing runs them.
The rest of $785B's states after a gap of three NOPs: 6 drops the stones like state 2 ($78AC); 3 sets the spikes; 4 raises them; 7 sets the trapdoors; 8 opens them in turn.
The RTS for a spike state with all three spikes up.
Two zero bytes after temple_trap_more; nothing reads them.

State 7 of the Temple's trap: three trapdoors (sprites 2-4, shape $BE, black, double height) in the floor at line $DA, X 96, 192 and 288, and $1D = 16 before the first opens; then state 8 ($79B6): every 32 calls the next one is switched on, open, until all three are.
The RTS of the trapdoor states while they wait.
The RTS for all three trapdoors open.
Seven zero bytes after temple_trapdoors; nothing reads them.

Reads the collision latch. Only the value 2 in its two low bits counts: the runner's lower half (sprite 1) touching something while the upper half (sprite 0) is not. Then the runner is caught: on the spikes it sinks to the floor and falls; at a trapdoor it moves over the open one (bit 2, 3 or 4 of the latch) and drops down through the floor; under spears or stones it is pushed down to the floor, the fallers drop on to line $E0, and the runner lies down (shapes $A0/$9F) beside where it stood. A long wait, every sprite off, a life lost ($02): the fifth ends the level at $1300, otherwise the tune restarts and the room starts again at $7600.
Four zero bytes after temple_caught; nothing reads them.

Level 7, the Bridge: sets the phase's colours ($1CDA), then (entered at $7B03 to restart after a lost life) the runner (sprites 0 and 1, shapes $90/$91, multicoloured) at X 112 high up at lines $58 and $6D; black border; the multicolour characters at $3000. Draws the gorge from $4C00-$4FE7: a byte with bit 7 set is that character in the phase's colour $5F, the rest in brown; every space from $0700 (row 19, column 8) to the end becomes a random character $E2-$E4 in orange. The six planks of the bridge (sprites 2-7, shape $B3, the phase's colour $5E, double width) are spaced across at line $70. Then the loop: the planks ($7C8A), the runner ($7D10), a delay of $5A (the phase's: 9 to 6) times 256; $2A = $A6 means five lives are lost (to $1300), $73 a life lost (the tune restarts, back to $7B03). Every 1024 passes the stage $45 and the music go up ($6530), and stage 9 wins ($1300).
One zero byte after bridge; nothing reads it.

Moves the six planks a pixel left. Every 52 calls ($11) the next plank in turn is put back at X 312 at the right: a plank with a hole (shape $B4) with an even chance, unless three holes have come in a row ($15), else a whole one (shape $B3).

The runner. On the bridge ($16 = 0): every 8 calls the legs move (shapes $90/$91 to $94/$95), the hole check ($7DD0), then the stick: down starts a low jump of $5B lines, left a middle one of $5C, up a high one of $5D (19, 32 and 44 lines in phase 1, a line less each phase). Every call with the stick held other than centred or fire alone counts an achievement in $68, also for right and the diagonals, which do not jump. In the air, every second call: rising a line a step (shapes $96/$97) for the jump's height, then falling (shapes $98/$99) as far, and the hole check after each.
